items.name: Niger seed oil
items.preparation: A regional cold-pressed oil; use fresh — its polyunsaturated profile ages poorly.

items.name: Mahua oil
items.prabhava: Solid tribal cooking fat pressed from mahua kernels — the ghee-substitute of central Indian forest kitchens.
contraindications: food-grade refined quality matters (crude oil carries saponins)
items.preparation: Used like vegetable ghee in its home regions; source food-grade pressed kernels.
provenance: Central Indian tribal tradition; madhuka lineage

items.name: Corn oil
contraindications: omega-6 heaviness as a sole daily oil — rotate with ghee/sesame/coconut
items.preparation: A characterless refined oil; acceptable workhorse, nothing more in the Ayurvedic ledger.

items.name: Soybean oil
combinations: bulk refined cooking (the default 'refined oil' of Indian shops)
contraindications: soy allergy (highly refined oil usually tolerated; caution stands)
items.preparation: The anonymous refined oil in most 'refined oil' bottles; rotate with traditional fats rather than defaulting to it.

items.name: Palm oil
items.prabhava: Two oils under one name — carotene-red unrefined palm (a traditional food) and the refined industrial fat of packaged snacks.
combinations: red palm: West African and coastal cooking traditions
contraindications: as hidden fat in packaged foods — the real exposure route
items.preparation: If using, choose unrefined red palm for its carotenes; the bigger Ayurvedic advice is noticing how much refined palm arrives uninvited in packets.
provenance: Modern global food system; regional traditions

items.name: Vanaspati (hydrogenated fat)
items.prabhava: Hydrogenated vegetable fat sold as ghee's cheap twin — carries trans fats with none of ghrita's virtues; the tradition it imitates argues against it.
combinations: none recommended — replace with real ghee or oil in any recipe that calls for it
contraindications: all doshas suffer; ama-forming by both classical and modern logic
avoid — recommendation engine must never suggest it
items.preparation: Included so users can identify and log it, not use it; every vanaspati recipe works better with ghee.
provenance: Modern industrial fat; WHO trans-fat guidance
items.reviewNote: Engine exclusion like betel nut: display with warning, never recommend.

items.name: Date palm jaggery (nolen gur)
items.prabhava: Bengal's winter treasure — fresh date-palm sap boiled to fragrant jaggery; cooler and finer than cane gur, the soul of winter sandesh and payesh.
contraindications: season-bound freshness (winter product; off-season 'nolen gur' is usually flavoring)
items.preparation: Use fresh in its winter window; heat gently — its aroma is volatile and is the entire point.

items.name: Palmyra jaggery (karupatti)
items.prabhava: Dark palmyra-sap jaggery of Tamil country — mineral-deep, classically cooling; the karupatti coffee sweetener and pathiya (convalescent-diet) sugar.
items.preparation: Grate or melt into drinks and sweets; Tamil tradition treats it as the medicinal jaggery.

items.name: Raw sugar (khand)
items.prabhava: The middle rung of the classical sugar ladder — between guda and refined sita; unbleached crystals keeping a trace of cane's minerals.
combinations: household sweetening where white sugar would go
items.preparation: Swap one-for-one with white sugar; the classical ladder ranks each step of refinement cooler but emptier.

items.name: Boora sugar
items.prabhava: Powdery re-crystallized khand — the prasad sugar of North Indian temples and the ladoo-binder of home kitchens.
combinations: besan and atta ladoos (it binds without wetness)
items.preparation: Its dry powder folds into ladoos where syrupy sugars fail; buy fresh — it cakes with humidity.

items.name: Coconut sugar
items.prabhava: Coconut-blossom sap sugar — caramel-toned, mineral-bearing; the modern wellness market's jaggery in Southeast Asian dress.
combinations: in baking and coffee as brown-sugar swap
items.preparation: Use like soft brown sugar; treat glycemic claims with the skepticism sugar always deserves.

items.name: Date syrup
items.prabhava: Whole dates reduced to pourable sweetness — closer to a fruit concentrate than a refined syrup; kharjura's building nature intact.
items.preparation: Choose pure pressed-date syrup without added sugar; a building sweetener in the kharjura line.

items.name: Aged honey
items.prabhava: Honey aged past a year — classical texts rank purana madhu the best scraper of kapha and fat; drier and more lekhana (scraping) than fresh.
combinations: warm (not hot) water in the morning (kapha-reduction tradition)
viruddha: heating or cooking (all honey rules apply)
items.preparation: Simply honey kept sealed past a year — crystallization is natural and harmless; all fresh-honey rules apply unchanged.

items.name: Sambhar lake salt
items.prabhava: Romaka — the lake salt of classical lists, historically from Sambhar; ranked light and quick-acting among the five salts.
combinations: general seasoning where rock salt is unavailable
items.preparation: A classical-list salt more than a market distinction today; saindhava (rock salt) remains the daily first choice.
provenance: Classical lavana pentad (saindhava, samudra, vida, sauvarchala, romaka)

items.name: Edible lime (chuna)
items.prabhava: Calcium hydroxide of the paan tradition — a wheat-grain-sized trace amount is the folk calcium supplement; alkali chemistry demands respect.
combinations: grain-sized dose in water or curd (folk calcium practice)
contraindications: caustic in quantity — strictly trace amounts
items.preparation: Wheat-grain quantities only, well mixed; this is an alkali handled by tradition with precision — the dose is the safety.

items.name: Baking soda
items.prabhava: The modern kitchen alkali — leavens dhokla and cakes, softens beans; Ayurvedically a kshara (alkali) to be used in pinches.
combinations: a pinch in hard-water bean pots
contraindications: destroys B-vitamins when overused in cooking vegetables
items.preparation: Pinch doses in batters; the traditional papad-khar and modern soda are cousins in the kshara family.

items.name: Edible acacia gum (gond)
items.prabhava: The winter laddu gum — gond crystals fried in ghee puff into crunchy building material; the classical postpartum and cold-season strengthener.
combinations: gond laddu with wheat flour, ghee, dry fruits (winter/postpartum)
contraindications: always fry before use (raw gum swells uncomfortably)
items.preparation: Fry crystals in ghee until they puff completely, then bind into laddus; the heating counterpart to cooling gond katira — don't confuse the two.
provenance: North Indian winter-postpartum tradition; babbula lineage

items.name: Tragacanth gum (gond katira, raw)
items.prabhava: The cooling gum crystal — soaks into voluminous jelly; summer's counterpart to winter's gond, and the two must never be swapped.
combinations: soaked overnight into sherbets and milk (see dravya.gond-katira-drink)
viruddha: frying it (that's winter gond's treatment — katira is soaked, never fried)
contraindications: always fully soaked with ample fluids (swells massively)
items.preparation: Soak a teaspoon of crystals overnight in ample water; identification matters — katira cools, babbula gond heats.

items.name: Edible silver leaf (vark)
items.prabhava: Gossamer silver on festive sweets — traditional rajata association with cooling and grace; nutritionally inert, ceremonially eloquent.
combinations: pressed onto barfi, kaju katli and paan
contraindications: adulteration is the real risk — aluminum foil passed as silver; buy certified (BIS) vark
strict vegetarians: traditional hammering between leather is now largely replaced — check certification
items.preparation: Apply the leaf directly from its backing paper onto the sweet; pure silver in these traces is biologically inert.
provenance: Mithai and paan tradition; rajata in rasashastra context
